cevap: I'm really glad to hear you're feeling "a bit better today" — that's worth noticing and holding onto. Small steps forward like this add up, and you deserve credit for getting here.
It takes real courage to say "I want to quit" out loud. That's your decision to make, and I'm here to support you however I can as you take it forward.
I'm glad you found a way to "relax a bit after the meeting" — that kind of relief matters. It sounds like the meeting gave you something worthwhile to hold onto.
Thank you for sharing that you're "not angry at anyone" right now. That's an honest place to be, and it's okay for your feelings to simply be what they are today.
Evenings can be tough, and it makes sense that you feel "a bit restless in the evenings." You're not alone in that, and we can think together about what might help those hours feel easier.
The fact that "this isn't my first attempt" says a lot about your persistence, not about failure. Every attempt teaches you something, and you're still here, still trying.
It's wonderful to hear that "things with my family got a bit better." Relationships take time to heal, and this sounds like a meaningful step in that direction.
Thank you for trusting me with something so personal — feeling "afraid of being alone" is more common than you might think. You don't have to carry that fear by yourself.
That's great news, that "my sleep schedule settled a bit." Rest can make such a difference in how everything else feels, so take that as real progress.
Feeling "ashamed to ask for help" is something a lot of people carry quietly, but reaching out here already shows strength. There's no shame in needing support.
I'm glad to hear "my appetite opened up a bit" — that's a good sign your body is finding some balance again. Small physical shifts like that are worth celebrating.
It's okay that "I didn't want to go that day" — those feelings are valid too, and you don't need to explain them away. What matters is that you're here now, talking about it.
